name: Tennis
description: Find your rhythm. One rally at a time.
safetyNote: Check the court, warm up gently, keep clear of others and stop if you feel pain.

resources.title: USTA Tennis 101
Intuitive Tennis: Beginner forehand and two-handed backhand (video)

upgrade.note: Your own graphite racquet, restringing, court shoes, lessons or clinics

name: Cycling / Fixed Gear
description: A little farther. A little more freedom.
safetyNote: Check air, brakes and chain before every ride. Use a fitted helmet and follow local traffic rules. Fixed-gear road use needs a functional front brake; do not learn brakeless street riding.

resources.title: Sheldon Brown: Fixed Gear for the Road
League of American Bicyclists: Learn to Ride (free course)

upgrade.note: Wheels, saddle, clipless pedals and shoes, a drivetrain refresh, a bike fit, tools

name: Swimming
description: Build confidence, one length at a time.
safetyNote: Practice with qualified supervision in a swim-safe environment. Never swim alone, hyperventilate or do breath-holding contests. Restrictive knee bands are not a default freestyle correction.

resources.title: Red Cross Adult Swim Lessons
MySwimPro: How to swim freestyle for beginners

upgrade.note: Better goggles, a training set, a swim watch, masters club or coached lessons

name: Journaling
description: Make a little space for your thoughts.

resources.title: Bullet Journal: How to start a simple bullet journal
UC Berkeley Greater Good in Action: Expressive writing

startSummary: Existing paper + pen · EASY TO START

upgrade.note: A hardcover or dot-grid notebook, a fountain pen and ink

name: PC Building
description: Understand the machine, then build it.
safetyNote: Unplug at the wall and hold the power button before opening anything. Ground yourself against the bare case or use a strap before touching a board, and never open a power supply — it holds charge long after it is unplugged.

resources.title: PCPartPicker Build Guides
Linus Tech Tips: How to build a PC (video)

upgrade.note: A faster graphics card, more memory, another drive, a monitor and peripherals

name: Drawing
safetyNote: Keep the wrist neutral and draw from the shoulder for large shapes. Take a short break every twenty to thirty minutes, work with light across the page, and stop if your hand aches.

resources.title: Drawabox Lesson 0: Getting started
Proko: Drawing Basics (video playlist)

startSummary: Pencil and paper · FREE TO TRY

upgrade.note: A quality sketchbook, graphite and charcoal, a drawing board, figure sessions, a tablet

name: Painting
description: Mix it, and see what the colour really is.
safetyNote: Work where air moves, keep solvents sealed and away from heat, and never pour them down a drain. Do not eat or point a brush with your mouth. Acrylic and watercolour avoid nearly all of this while you learn.

resources.title: The Art Sherpa: Beginner acrylic painting course
Will Kemp Art School: Acrylic painting for beginners

startSummary: Three colours + a brush · LOW COST

upgrade.note: Artist-grade paint, stretched canvas, an easel, better brushes, classes

name: Running
description: Slower than you think. Further than you expect.
safetyNote: Build distance gradually and take a lighter week roughly every fourth. Run facing traffic where there is no path, wear something reflective in low light, plan water in heat, and treat new sharp pain as a reason to stop.

resources.title: RRCA 10-week training plan for new runners
NHS: Get running with Couch to 5K

upgrade.note: A second pair for rotation, a GPS watch, race entries, coaching

name: Volleyball
description: Three touches, and everyone is involved.
safetyNote: Warm the shoulders, wrists and ankles before hitting. Set with firm fingers, land on two feet, keep out of the space under the net, and call loudly so nobody collides.

resources.title: USA Volleyball: A beginner's guide (PDF)
Elevate Yourself: Volleyball tutorials (video)

upgrade.note: Your own competition ball, court shoes, better pads, league fees

name: Reading
safetyNote: Read with light on the page rather than behind it, hold the book near eye level, and look at something distant every twenty minutes. Dim screens in the evening and prefer paper near bedtime.

resources.title: Libby: Getting started with free library ebooks
Book Riot: How to start reading (if you've never liked it)

startSummary: A library card · FREE TO TRY

upgrade.note: An e-reader, an audiobook subscription, a book budget, shelves
